note: P4317 (Pro 28:7) — who keeps the law is a discerning son; a companion of gluttons shames his father.

dims.v: discernment — the law-keeping son who honours his father
the understanding of the son who keeps the law — the discernment that both obeys and honours, the opposite of the shameful companion of gluttons
the shame it is set against (266727)
set against the son who shames his father
bin (understand/discern) — 'the one who keeps the law is a son with UNDERSTANDING'; law-keeping is the mark of a discerning son, and an honour to his father. Obedience and understanding go together.
dishonour — the son who disgraces his father by bad company
the shame a son brings on his father by being a companion of gluttons — dissolute company disgracing the parent, the reverse of the discerning son's honour
the understanding it is set against (266724)
set against the discerning son who honours his father
kalam (shame/disgrace) — 'but a companion of gluttons SHAMES his father'; the son who runs with the dissolute disgraces his parent. Company chosen reflects on the family (cf 23:20-21; 29:3).
